filename: Financial losses associated with US floods occur with frequent low-return-period precipitation.pdf
title: Financial losses associated with US floods occur with frequent low-return-period precipitation
code_availability: All associated project code in Python and RStudio for data preprocessing, analysis and evaluation is available via GitHub at https://github.com/adamnayak/USA_return_periods.
testbed_rationale: The study focuses on hydroclimatological statistical analysis and spatiotemporal clustering of historical financial flood losses and precipitation events, not on climate physical parameterization or emulation testbeds.
pain_points: Subdaily and county-level spatial averaging smooths rainfall fields in localized damage-inducing events
Discrepancies in multi-decadal trends between different precipitation reanalysis datasets (e.g., ERA5 vs. MSWEP)
DBSCAN/ST-DBSCAN parameterization sensitivity and difficulty validating threshold parameters
Human error and temporal reporting lags (up to 60 days) in FEMA claim and disaster declaration dates relative to physical precipitation events
extraction_notes: The machine learning aspect of this study is unsupervised spatiotemporal clustering (DBSCAN and ST-DBSCAN) used to group damage records and precipitation into synoptically driven storm events across space and time.
